content.text:
The abstract class approach is the right fit here. An interface can't have no-op defaults for two methods and still be a `@FunctionalInterface`, so subclasses would be forced to implement both even if they only care about one event — exactly the clutter the task wants to avoid. An abstract class with no-op defaults means a logging callback only overrides `onFound`, and an analytics callback overrides both.

The key addition is `andThen`: a `final` composition method mirroring `Function.andThen()` from the standard library. It lets multiple concerns chain onto a single callback reference without touching `BinarySearchTree` at all.

`BinarySearchTree` needs no structural changes — only `main` updates to demonstrate the composition.

content.text:
Each search fires both subscribers in sequence — `logger` then `analytics` — with no changes to `BinarySearchTree`. Here's what changed and why:

**`SearchCallback.java`** — Three targeted changes from the interface. First, the two abstract methods become concrete no-op implementations, so subclasses only override the events they care about: `logger` could silence `onNotFound` entirely, and neither override would cause a compile error. Second, `noOp()` simplifies to `new SearchCallback<T>() {}` — an empty anonymous subclass that inherits both no-ops. Third, `andThen(SearchCallback<T> next)` is a `final` composition method: it returns a new anonymous subclass that fires `self` then `next` for each event. `final` prevents subclasses from redefining the composition semantics. Access modifiers shift from the implicit `public` of interface methods to package-private, consistent with everything else in this package.

**`binary_search_tree_searching.java`** (`main` only) — The single `logger` is joined by an `analytics` callback that maintains stateful hit/miss counters — something that would have required a separate mechanism before. `logger.andThen(analytics)` produces a single `SearchCallback<T>` that the builder accepts, and `BinarySearchTree` is completely unaware there are two subscribers. Adding a third concern (a UI update callback, for instance) is one more `.andThen(uiCallback)` with zero changes elsewhere.
